q: In a metallic bond, the valence electrons of the atoms are very loosely held, forming a common _____ cloud.
e: Metallic bonding involves a shared cloud of delocalised valence electrons.

q: These mobile electrons in metallic bonding are often described as a "sea of _____".
e: The delocalised valence electrons are commonly referred to as a sea of electrons.

q: The positively charged metallic nuclei are surrounded by _____ electrons.
e: The sea of electrons in a metal is free to move throughout the lattice.

q: Metals consist of giant structures of atoms that are packed closely together in a regular arrangement called a _____.
e: Metal atoms form a closely packed regular arrangement known as a lattice.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing positive charge on the ions in the metal _____.
e: Higher ionic charges in the metal lattice lead to stronger electrostatic attractions.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the _____ size of metal ions in the lattice.
e: Smaller metal ions bring the nuclei closer to the sea of electrons, increasing bond strength.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing number of _____ electrons per atom.
e: More mobile valence electrons contributed per atom strengthen the metallic bond.

q: The strength of metallic bond is _____ than that of an ionic bond.
e: Generally, metallic bonds are weaker and have lower bond strengths than ionic bonds.

q: Consequently, the melting points of some metals become _____ compared with the ionic compounds.
e: Because metallic bonds are generally weaker than ionic bonds, many metals have lower melting points than ionic solids.

q: The bonding in metals results from the interaction of the mobile electrons with the various nuclei, hence they are held together by a strong _____ attraction.
e: Metallic bonding relies on the electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and negative delocalised electrons.
